scope: one saved-moving RHS control at archived solve3 point; baseline current g/SSD/count/cost and raw fixed must be exact before one sampler; no solver/native/raw MRI/GPU

lambda_policy.native_Lambda_definition: latest_ssd*lambda when ssd_lambda enabled; cf updates latest_ssd; grad uses it without computing a new SSD

limitations: Baseline bridges current frozen FNIT saved preprocessing, not identical official preprocessing.
Native samepoint effective lambda is saved and equal; native SSD is not separately saved, so an inferred quotient is not its bitexact identity.
Moving substitution holds lambda fixed despite new SSD; it does not reproduce a fresh native ssd-weighted objective or prove native equivalence.
The fixed image is unscaled Ref(); a phase/value mismatch stops without forced normalization or rescaling.
FSL-order control retains FNIT projection and separable adjoint; it does not match every official sum or derivative operation.
Bending gradient is computed once at the saved coefficients from saved optimized Gram state; bending energy is the previously verified scalar, not a new energy evaluation.
No native solve3 warp/mask/partial/Jte/bending subcomponents are stored; total-g comparison cannot identify a unique cause.
Three coefficient blocks and scale have mixed parameter units; errors are not voxel displacements.
Source/input/hash/import and cold JIT wall observations are not a performance ratio.
Before/after mapped DSO identities are snapshots, not a full-time system-call or loader audit.
No solver, topology, final warp, full-registration validation or production CPU/GPU change.
fixed_phase: Ref() before global scaling; same raw F32 values, no phase conversion
full_g_units: positive full g=2*FNIT half-gradient; three 392 coefficient blocks plus one dimensionless global scale, not voxel errors
